defect.description: The backward-incompatible crash: kwargs.pop('method', form.method).upper() raises AttributeError when a caller passes method=None explicitly, which used to work (Request turns a None method into GET); the change should treat None like a missing method.

review_items: src/forms.py:43 — method=None kwarg raises AttributeError (regression from old None→GET handling)
src/forms.py:33 — valid_form_methods is a mutable list class attribute; use a tuple
src/forms.py:43 — redundant uppercase, also done in Request.__post_init__
votes.evidence_quote: `kwargs.pop("method", form.method)` returns the explicit `None` value when the caller passes `method=None`, not the default. Then `None.upper()` raises.
votes.justification: The review names the exact defect: passing method=None explicitly makes from_form raise AttributeError. It also notes this is a regression, since the old code passed None through to Request, which turns it into GET.
